title: Avoid alcohol while taking NSAIDs (gastrointestinal bleeding)
summary: Combining NSAIDs with alcohol markedly increases the risk of stomach bleeding; avoid use within 8–10 hours before and after drinking.
applicable_scene: Adding an NSAID medication; food-avoidance list initialization (seed supply); prompt when a meal containing alcohol is selected in diet logging
source_name: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) patient education material ⚠️ (gi.org returned 403 this time, so it could not be verified directly; marked as unverified)

payload.risk: Both damage the gastric mucosa; together they increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding
payload.timing: Avoid NSAIDs within 8–10 hours before and after drinking alcohol
evidence: Shanghai Municipal Health Commission: NSAIDs should be avoided in the 8–10 hours before and after drinking alcohol, so as not to increase the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.
ACG patient material: They should not be taken with alcohol, as the combination can increase the risk of GI bleeding.
action: For long-term NSAID users: the food-avoidance list includes "alcohol (strict)" by default
On days with social drinking: switch that dose of pain relief to the doctor-approved alternative; do not add an extra NSAID on the spot
After alcohol is marked in diet logging, that day's medication card shows a staggered-timing prompt

title: During steroid therapy: limit salt, supplement potassium and calcium, watch grapefruit
summary: During steroid treatment such as prednisone, your doctor may recommend a low-salt, high-potassium / high-calcium diet and calcium supplements; ask your doctor before drinking grapefruit juice.
applicable_scene: Adding a glucocorticoid; diet-logging reference during long-term steroid therapy; nutrient plan suggestions
source_name: MedlinePlus prednisone patient medication information (U.S. National Library of Medicine)

payload.risk: Without limiting sodium: risk of edema and elevated blood pressure; calcium loss (long term)
evidence: MedlinePlus: Your doctor may instruct you to follow a low-salt, high potassium, or high calcium diet. Your doctor may also prescribe or recommend a calcium or potassium supplement.
MedlinePlus: Talk to your doctor about eating grapefruit and drinking grapefruit juice while you are taking this medication.
action: Low-salt diet (bland flavors; cut back on pickled foods / heavily salted takeout meals)
Add high-potassium foods (bananas / oranges / spinach, etc.) and high-calcium foods (dairy / soy products) as recipe tags
Grapefruit / grapefruit juice: ask your doctor before consuming while taking steroids
Nutrient plan and follow-up confirmation: whether calcium + vitamin D supplementation is needed follows the doctor's orders
payload.app_link: recipes tag system (high_calcium / low_salt); supplements (calcium / vitamin D) suggestions; grapefruit (avoid) can be added to the food-avoidance list

title: Avoid alcohol while taking methotrexate
summary: Both methotrexate and alcohol are hepatotoxic, and combining them compounds the risk; patient education advises people taking MTX to stop drinking, and to discuss any intake with their doctor.
applicable_scene: Food-avoidance list seed supply when methotrexate is added; prompt when alcohol is marked in diet logging
source_name: EMA methotrexate oral solution product information ⚠️ (the EMA site connection was reset this time, the referrals path returned 404 in testing, and no accessible link could be verified; marked as unverified)

payload.risk: Additive hepatotoxicity (both cause liver injury); the literature indicates that with >100g of alcohol per week the risk of severe liver disease is about 3%, and higher when other liver-disease risk factors are present
evidence: Clin Exp Rheumatol: Hepatotoxicity is associated with both alcohol and methotrexate.
GoodRx patient education: It's a standard recommendation to stop drinking alcohol if you've been prescribed methotrexate.
EMA product information: the most serious adverse reactions of methotrexate include hepatotoxicity, with abnormal liver function tests commonly seen.
action: The food-avoidance list includes "alcohol (strict)" by default (displayed merged with fdg-001)
If complete abstinence is not possible, discuss an acceptable amount with your doctor (UK rheumatologists' recommendations vary — individualize)
Liver function monitoring (linked to checkup_items lab)
payload.app_link: food_avoid_items(seed: alcohol×strict); cross-linked within the itx-001 once-weekly item group

title: During leflunomide treatment: the label advises stopping alcohol, with regular liver enzyme monitoring
summary: The Chinese leflunomide label states clearly "stop drinking alcohol during treatment"; check ALT every 2 weeks for the first 6 months, then every 8 weeks.
applicable_scene: Prompt when leflunomide is added; reminder when liver enzyme retesting is due
source_name: Chinese-language leflunomide tablet label (indexed by **Yaozhi Data (药智数据), a commercial drug database**; the link for this entry is that index page — a commercial platform); parallel citations: EMA Leflunomide Mylan product information ⚠️ (that EMA EPAR path returned 404 in testing) and Health Canada Product Monograph ⚠️ (not checked); the latter two are both marked as unverified

payload.risk: Additive hepatotoxic effects (as stated in the label); if ALT stays above 2 times the limit / exceeds 3 times the limit, the drug must be stopped + a washout procedure is required
payload.timing: Throughout treatment (monitoring: q2w for the first 6 months → q8w thereafter)
evidence: Chinese-language label: because additive hepatotoxic effects are possible, it is recommended to stop drinking alcohol during leflunomide treatment.
EMA: ALT (SGPT) must be checked before initiation... every two weeks during the first six months of treatment and every 8 weeks thereafter.
Health Canada: contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment; not recommended for patients who are HBV/HCV positive or have pre-existing liver disease.
action: Adding leflunomide → checkup_items automatically suggests ALT monitoring items (q2w × 6 months → q8w)
The food-avoidance list includes alcohol (strict) by default
When a history of liver disease / positive hepatitis B or C is entered, this entry raises a red_flag for the doctor
payload.app_link: checkup_items (automatic ALT interval suggestion); food_avoid_items(seed: alcohol×strict); together with the itx-005 sulfasalazine entry, part of the csDMARD medication key-points group

title: Grapefruit interactions with some medications: check before you take them
summary: Grapefruit juice blocks the intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme and can raise blood levels of some drugs abnormally high; for JAK inhibitors and others that explicitly say to avoid it, and for other drugs follow the label.
applicable_scene: When adding a JAK inhibitor / a CYP3A4 substrate drug such as tacrolimus; food-avoidance list seed supply
source_name: FDA consumer information "Grapefruit Juice and Some Drugs Don't Mix" (2021); Upadacitinib patient education (NCBI Bookshelf) (all evidence quotes in this entry come from this source: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/grapefruit-juice-and-some-drugs-dont-mix)

payload.risk: Grapefruit blocks intestinal CYP3A4 → increased absorption and higher blood levels of some oral drugs (too much drug in your body); Seville oranges / pomelos / tangelos carry the same risk
payload.timing: Throughout the period of taking the relevant drug (not only at the moment of dosing)
evidence: FDA: Grapefruit juice can block the action of intestinal CYP3A4, so instead of being metabolized, more of the drug enters the blood and stays in the body longer.
FDA: Seville oranges, pomelos, and tangelos might have the same effect as grapefruit juice.
Upadacitinib patient education: Patients should avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit-containing products during upadacitinib treatment.
action: Adding a JAK inhibitor (upadacitinib, etc.) → the food-avoidance list includes grapefruit (strict) by default
Other drugs: check the "Interactions" section of the label / ask a pharmacist (do not assume every rheumatology drug is affected)
Also watch foods containing pomelo/citrus ingredients (pomelo tea / jam)
payload.app_link: medications(risk_tags) cyp3a4-tagged drug addition trigger; food_avoid_items seed supply; displayed merged with the fdg-002 steroid grapefruit prompt

title: Long-term glucocorticoids: watch protein and calcium intake together
summary: With long-term steroid therapy, protein breakdown increases and calcium loss accelerates — dietary high-quality protein and calcium intake both need attention (a supplementary layer to the MedlinePlus dietary advice).
applicable_scene: Recipe recommendation tags for users on long-term steroid therapy (>3 months); nutrient plan suggestions
source_name: MedlinePlus prednisone patient medication information (U.S. National Library of Medicine, NLM, a government agency page; same URL as fdg-002); the second source is a nutrition review (journal; the specific article could not be verified, marked as unverified)

payload.risk: Long-term steroids: protein breakdown / calcium loss (osteoporosis direction) — not a contraindication warning but a supplementation direction
evidence: MedlinePlus prednisone patient medication information (https://medlineplus.gov/druginfo/meds/a601102.html, an NLM government agency page; same source as fdg-002): Your doctor may also prescribe or recommend a calcium or potassium supplement. (linked to fdg-002)

⚠️ unverified: an existing excerpt in this entry states "nutrition review summary: for people on long-term glucocorticoids, optimizing calcium intake to 1000–1200 mg/day and vitamin D to 600–800 IU/day is recommended"; the specific article and source of that review could not be verified this time, so it is not treated as a traceable citation. 1000–1200 mg/day, vitamin D 600–800 IU/day, and maintain adequate protein intake.
action: Recipe tags: prioritize high_calcium / high_protein recommendations (for long-term steroid users)
Nutrient plan: whether to supplement calcium + vitamin D follows the doctor's orders (a follow-up visit topic)
Weight management in parallel (linked to weight_logs)
payload.app_link: recipes tag linkage; supplements (calcium / vitamin D) suggestion items; cross-linked within the fdg-002 group
